History:
• Chief complaint: Loose, watery diarrhea for the past 3 days.  
• Frequency: ~6–7 bowel movements/day.  
• Associated symptoms: Intermittent crampy left-lower-abdominal pain, initial episode of vomiting (resolved), subjective fever at onset, weakness/shakiness, loss of appetite.  
• No blood in stool or vomit; no current fever, no night sweats.  
• Able to tolerate fluids; taking mainly soups/smoothies.  
• Possible trigger: Chinese restaurant takeaway eaten 4 days ago.  
• Impact: Needs to remain near a toilet; continues working as an accountant but with difficulty.  
• Social history: Non-smoker, does not drink alcohol.  
• Family: One child had brief vomiting only; no similar diarrhea in household.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma—well controlled with inhaler.  
• Medications: Inhaler (type/dose/frequency not documented); no other regular medicines.  
• Allergies: Not documented.  
• No prior gastrointestinal disorders reported.

Physical Examination:
• Encounter conducted via consultation; no formal exam performed.  
• Patient alert, conversational; reports weakness.  
• No reported blood in stool or vomit.  
• No current fever reported; vitals not obtained.

Impression:
• Acute gastroenteritis, likely viral or food-borne bacterial, following recent takeaway meal.

Management Plan:
• Conservative management advised:
  – Oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte), as directed by pharmacy.  
  – Continue liberal oral fluids and light diet.  
  – Paracetamol 2 tablets (dose/strength not documented) up to four times daily for fever or pain.  
• Rest: Take 2–3 days off work to aid recovery.  
• Return precautions: If symptoms persist beyond 3–4 days, worsen, or if blood appears in stool/vomit, high fever, or inability to keep fluids down, seek reassessment.  
• Possible future investigations: Stool sample and further tests if no improvement.  
• Follow-up: Telephone or in-person review if not better in 3–4 days.

Patient Summary:
Middle-aged man with well-controlled asthma presents with 3 days of watery diarrhea, intermittent left-sided abdominal cramps, brief early vomiting, and mild systemic symptoms after eating takeaway food. Clinical picture consistent with uncomplicated acute gastroenteritis. Supportive care and close follow-up arranged.

Key Takeaways:
1. Stay well hydrated; use oral rehydration salts from the pharmacy.  
2. Rest at home for the next 2–3 days and take paracetamol as needed.  
3. Contact the clinic if not improved in 3–4 days or if concerning symptoms develop.

Next Steps:
• Begin oral rehydration solution today.  
• Paracetamol for symptomatic relief.  
• Re-assessment in 3–4 days if diarrhea not resolving; stool culture may be ordered then.
